summary.text: Don Beyer is the Democratic incumbent seeking a seventh term representing Virginia's 8th District. A longtime Northern Virginia auto-dealership owner, he served as Lieutenant Governor of Virginia and as U.S. Ambassador to Switzerland and Liechtenstein before entering Congress in 2015. He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the Joint Economic Committee and campaigns on opposing the Trump administration's tariffs and tax cuts and expanding affordable housing and health coverage.

paragraphs.text: Beyer was born in 1950 in the Free Territory of Trieste, the son of a U.S. Army officer, and was raised in Washington, D.C.
He graduated from Gonzaga College High School, where he was named a Presidential Scholar, and earned a bachelor's degree from Williams College.
After a summer job at a car dealership in 1974, he spent four decades building his family's auto business in Northern Virginia, which Wikipedia reports he sold to his brother in 2019.
He was also a co-founder of the Northern Virginia Technology Council.

Beyer served as Lieutenant Governor of Virginia from 1990 to 1998, with signature work on advocacy for Virginians with disabilities and protections for vulnerable residents during the state's mid-1990s welfare reform.
He was the Democratic nominee for governor in 1997 and lost to Jim Gilmore.
He spent 14 years as chair of Jobs for Virginia Graduates, a high school dropout-prevention program, and chaired the Virginia Economic Recovery Commission.

Nominated by President Obama, he served as U.S. Ambassador to Switzerland and Liechtenstein from 2009 to 2013, advocating for stricter sanctions on Iran and working with the Justice Department on Swiss bank-secrecy abuses.
Beyer won the 2014 Democratic primary for the open 8th District seat held by retiring Rep. Jim Moran, then the general election, and has been re-elected five times since.
In the House he serves on the Committee on Ways and Means and on the Joint Economic Committee, which he chaired in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).
According to his official biography, he and his wife Megan live in Alexandria, Virginia, and he has four children and two grandchildren.
